title: Candidate prompt change displaced the intended editorial hierarchy and triggered a rollback
description: A single added section in the Narrative user prompt — intended to “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis” — produced consistent, repeatable degradations in both Narrative and Compose outputs: company-level identity and audience were subordinated while orchestration became central, unsupported claims appeared, and the change was not promoted. The production prompt was restored byte-for-byte.
audience: Prompt engineers, editorial leads, release managers
rationale: This experiment shows a straightforward operational risk: even a small, generic prompt change can reliably alter high-level emphasis and introduce editorial regressions that fail promotion gates. Teams deciding whether to change system prompts need evidence that a change preserves the intended hierarchy before promoting it.
evidence: Facts: the candidate prompt added one generic section titled “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis” and contained no Nuëyon-specific wording; three candidate Narrative runs scored mean 4.00/10 vs baseline mean 6.00/10; three candidate Compose runs scored mean 3.33/10 vs baseline mean 5.67/10; all candidate Narrative and Compose runs made orchestration central and introduced unsupported additions; decision: “Do not promote. Candidate was worse on mean score… failed the orchestration hierarchy and factual restraint gates in every run,” and production prompt was restored (byte-for-byte SHA match). Inference: the added prompt section correlated with the observed editorial drift and regressions. Unknowns: the exact causal mechanism inside the model that produced the drift (e.g., how the new phrasing interacted with the Synthesis content or model internals).
